brief: The Market Ear's weekly wrap strings together several extremes. SPX broke its 200-day moving average, then its longer-term trendline, and now trades below 7,000 in futures, with RSI at its most oversold since the Liberation Day panic. MS prime brokerage data puts US long/short hedge fund net exposure at 42%, an 8th percentile reading since 2010 that historically coincides with 5% median SPX earnings growth. Current consensus instead expects 16% growth next year, a disconnect between positioning and expectations. Separately, GS prime brokerage data shows hedge funds dumping Asian AI/tech exposure, with long sales outpacing shorts 2.4 to 1, concentrated in Korea and Taiwan. Korea allocation is back to January levels, and Taiwan allocation has fallen to a 24th percentile. A EWT December 95 put recommended under a month ago to play a Taiwan catch-down has risen from $2 to almost $20. DB separately argues India can benefit from AI adoption rather than invention, citing its 1.5 billion potential users. Gold and silver are both extremely oversold, gold's RSI near decade lows and silver's RSI down from 90 to 30, with gold volatility spiking as the metal fails to find a bid.
